pr.title: Declare defaults for the accessibility signal delay settings
pr.body:
Fixes #286430

## Problem

The three `accessibility.signalOptions.experimental.delays.*` settings (`general`, `warningAtPosition`, `errorAtPosition`) are `object` settings that declare `default` values on their properties only, without a `default` for the setting itself. The configuration registry therefore registers an empty object as the default:

- The settings editor renders an empty table with an "Add Item" button instead of the default rows, and "Preferences: Open Default Settings (JSON)" shows `{}` for the three settings.
- `AccessibilitySignalService.getDelayMs` reads `value.sound` and `value.announcement` from that empty object when the settings are not configured, so the documented delays are not applied.

These are the only object settings in the core that rely on property level defaults alone.

## Fix

Declare the object defaults explicitly, using the values already documented on the properties (`announcement: 3000`, `sound: 400` for general, `sound: 1000` for the two position signals). The settings editor now shows the default rows, and the runtime default matches the documentation. Users who configured the settings themselves are not affected.

## How to test

1. Open the settings editor and search for `accessibility.signalOptions.experimental.delays`.
2. Before this change: each of the three settings shows an empty table with an "Add Item" button.
3. After this change: each setting lists its `announcement` and `sound` rows with the default values, and "Preferences: Open Default Settings (JSON)" shows the objects instead of `{}`.

commit.message:
Declare defaults for the accessibility signal delay settings

The three accessibility.signalOptions.experimental.delays settings only
declared defaults on their object properties, so the registered default of
each setting was an empty object. The settings editor rendered an empty
table with an "Add Item" button instead of the default rows, and
getDelayMs read the delay values from an empty object when the settings
were not configured.

Declare the object defaults explicitly so both the settings editor and the
runtime see the documented values.

Fixes #286430
